reasons: Proof mismatch: fix-response.md's Round 4 section states this round 'made no code change' and 'Checked each item against the current tree before touching anything' (confirming items 4-9 unapplied 'by grep', without touching the files). But evidence/hook-log.jsonl -- a literal, append-only tool-call log, not a claim -- records real Edit-tool invocations, all allowed (test_file_lock/protected_paths/secrets_check/format_on_edit all 'verdict: allow'), on exactly three files at 2026-10-08T11:38:30Z, 11:38:34Z and 11:38:37Z: plugin/gate/artifacts.py, plugin/gate/checks.py and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md -- the same three files that carry the deferred 'items 4-9' content (the 'eval (' comments at artifacts.py:89/checks.py:1637 and the OPERATING_MODEL.md:144 wording) the round's own narrative says it left untouched. This is squarely inside the fix round's own session window (after the owner's 11:27:20 iterations reset, before the 11:40:40 run-start and the 11:43:16 edit to fix-response.md itself), so it cannot be attributed to an earlier round.

I spot-checked the three specific lines the round's narrative names (artifacts.py:89, checks.py:1637, OPERATING_MODEL.md:144) and their current on-disk text does match the 'still unapplied / still reads eval (' claim, and git status at the start of this review shows no uncommitted diff on these three files (only diff-e.patch and hook-log.jsonl are 'M'), so whatever the Edit calls changed was either reverted within the same session before the commit, or is a no-op I have not located elsewhere in two large files (checks.py is 1600+ lines) I have not byte-diffed in full against the pre-round-4 commit. Without git access I cannot rule out a stray, undocumented change to either file beyond the three lines I checked.

Even on the most charitable reading (the edits were fully reverted and nothing in the two files actually changed), the round's committed record is not an accurate account of what the session did: it asserts it only read/grepped these files when the tool log shows it edited them. That is exactly the kind of claim-vs-toolchain-evidence gap this review is supposed to catch, and it is the owner's call whether to accept the explanation or ask the run to reconcile fix-response.md with hook-log.jsonl before this round is taken as 'nothing new to apply'.
classification_reasons: Blast radius: plugin/gate/checks.py's lesson_and_eval/_supersedes_problem gates every entry_route:incident change at gate (e) for every project on this plugin version; this change also edits docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md (process documentation of the contract) and ships a new generated-index subsystem (plugin/lessons/index.py) -- several independent pieces of behavior, not a small patch.

The spec carried one open concern through multiple rounds (the Windows newline/CRLF mechanism was reopened once already) and this fix round itself surfaced a process defect (a double iteration bump past the non-routine cap) requiring an owner label to clear -- not a tight, single-pass spec.

New, previously-uncovered code paths (supersedes path/shape validation, frontmatter bad-field-shape handling) were added with new tests in recent rounds; this round's own hook-log discrepancy (above) is exactly the kind of untested-by-the-suite, human-judgment gap non-routine classification exists to catch.
attempted: Intent: round 4's stated purpose (apply the owner's sdlc:reset-iterations, re-check the two still-open PR review threads, conclude both were already resolved or owner-deferred) matches intent.md/spec.md's scope; no drift from the stated problem in what the round claims to have done.

Spec and plan: spec.md and plan.md already carry every requirement and fail case from prior rounds (verified against the first adversarial pass's own citations); this round adds no new requirement and the diff-e.patch stat for plan.md/spec.md shows no further change beyond what prior rounds already landed, consistent with 'no spec/plan change this round'.

Proof: compared fix-response.md's Round 4 narrative against evidence/hook-log.jsonl tool-call records for the exact time window of this round (after the 11:27:20 reset). Found the mismatch described above: Edit-tool calls to plugin/gate/artifacts.py, plugin/gate/checks.py and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md that the narrative never mentions and that contradict its 'nothing new to apply' / 'checked ... before touching anything' framing. test.log/build.log/lint.log remain correctly 'deferred to the runner' (unchanged, consistent with no code change being intended); verifier.md is the prior round's (00ddfc7) report and is appropriate to leave standing only if this round truly changed nothing -- which is exactly what the hook-log discrepancy puts in doubt.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, this repo's root sdlc.yaml) touched. template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are plugin-shipped content per plan.md's own citation, not this repo's guardrails. No sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies.

Policies: REVIEW.md's 'Framework rules' (plan.md must reflect the diff; second-occurrence rule) are addressed in review-response.md/claude-md-proposals.md from the prior round and are owner-deferred, not re-litigated here. No new stored personal/sensitive field.

Tests: no pre-existing test was weakened in this change overall (confirmed in the prior round's review, unchanged here); this round added no test of its own, consistent with its claim of no code change -- which makes the undisclosed Edit-tool activity on source files, with no accompanying test change, the more notable gap, since a real edit to checks.py/artifacts.py with no test delta would itself be a definition-of-done violation if it had landed.
